slice: FULL SAIL Stage 1 NIGHTWATCH Ch4 Slice C1

findings.red: After 088-095, an arbitrary LOGIN with only ambient public-schema USAGE can EXECUTE public-schema functions that still default-grant PUBLIC (pgcrypto, trigger helpers, business functions). Direct ACL audit cannot see PUBLIC. Trusted-precreated pregrant audit therefore refuses adoption.
findings.green: Canonical 096, run as the queue table/function owner, REVOKE EXECUTE ON ALL FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC. A LOGIN with only ambient public USAGE cannot execute any non-explicit public-schema function. Function owners keep implicit EXECUTE. Existing explicit GRANT EXECUTE to named roles survive. 096 does not GRANT the worker or name live roles/UUIDs.

findings.red: PostgreSQL default privileges keep granting EXECUTE to PUBLIC on newly created functions, so a later CREATE FUNCTION or CREATE EXTENSION by the same owner reopens ambient execute.
findings.green: 096 ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES FOR ROLE <applying owner> IN SCHEMA public REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTIONS FROM PUBLIC. Existing and newly created functions owned by that role default non-PUBLIC. Owner nuance: default privileges do not bind another owner; an extension script that GRANT EXECUTE TO PUBLIC explicitly can reintroduce ambient execute. The principal ambient audit still fail-closes on reintroduction. Procedures are outside ALL FUNCTIONS.

findings.red: Live Sunset staging trusted-precreated worker adoption correctly refused because pregrant audit found dozens of effective public-schema functions callable through ambient PUBLIC EXECUTE. The worker LOGIN stayed parked NOLOGIN with no mapping/grants.
findings.green: After 096, automation principal audit/adoption permits only the contract allowlist. Re-GRANT EXECUTE TO PUBLIC on any public-schema function is still rejected by the ambient PUBLIC audit. No runtime flags, provider, or live role changes.
